lines: Imagine falling from the sky through a violent storm and waking up alone in a deadly jungle.
On 24 December 1971 a passenger plane is struck by lightning and breaks apart midair.
Seventeen year old Juliane Koepcke falls about 3000 meters while still strapped to her seat row.
She wakes up on the dark forest floor with a broken collarbone and a deep arm cut.
She also suffers from a painful eye injury and a severe concussion after the terrifying plunge.
Her biologist father previously taught her that following flowing water always leads back to people.
She finds a tiny creek and begins walking through the dense and dangerous Peruvian rainforest.
Days pass slowly as she follows the winding water toward a larger and safer river.
Up to 14 other passengers survive the initial crash but tragically die before any rescue arrives.
She spends 11 long days completely alone in the unforgiving jungle facing unimaginable odds.
After 9 days of difficult travel she finally discovers a remote lumberjack camp by the river.
She is found by local workers who provide medical help and bring her back to safety.
Juliane remains the only official survivor of LANSA Flight 508 against all odds and expectations.
Would you have the mental strength to survive 11 days alone in the dangerous rainforest?

lines: If your car breaks down in the desert heat, do not panic and start walking.
Mark needs to survive the brutal daytime temperatures before the sun goes down completely today.
The relentless heat strikes immediately, baking the empty landscape and threatening his life right now.
One. Stay with the broken car because a vehicle is much easier to spot than a person.
Mark raises the hood of the car to signal any passing rescue teams in the distance.
Two. Rest in the shade during the hottest hours of the day to avoid heatstroke.
Mark walks to the large rock for shelter and sits down out of the direct sun.
He uses a mirror to flash sunlight toward the horizon while keeping his phone safe.
Three. Drink the water you have when thirsty because rationing water while you overheat does not help.
He drinks from his bottle immediately because waiting makes dehydration much worse.
Mark waves his hands to signal again while staying safely near the protective rock shade.
He must wait for the evening to move because moving during the day is deadly.
The shade protects him from the worst of the daytime temperatures as hours pass slowly.
It was the perfect survival plan in the middle of the unforgiving desert.
There was just one problem when the phone screen suddenly flickered and died completely.
part1.cliffhanger: The phone battery dies completely right before he can call for help.
